I've written five draft examples for **Sick leave notes** and saved them to the idea. They're **not approved yet**, and nothing can be built until you and the owner of staff health data say yes. I couldn't ask you questions in this session, so I haven't decided anything for you.

## Draft examples

1. When I open "Sick leave", fill in first day 6 Oct 2026, last day 7 Oct 2026 and diagnosis "Flu", and press "Record sick leave", I see "Sick leave recorded" and the entry appears in my own list.
2. When someone in HR opens "Sick leave", they see every staff member's entries in one list, newest first, with name, first day, last day and diagnosis (e.g. "Jane Doe, 6 Oct 2026 – 7 Oct 2026, Flu").
3. When I press "Record sick leave" with no first day, I see "Please enter the first day" and nothing is added.
4. When I enter a last day before the first day, I see "The last day can't be before the first day" and nothing is added.
5. When a staff member who isn't in HR opens "Sick leave", they see only their own entries and never anyone else's name or diagnosis.

## What will change

- There will be a new "Sick leave" page in the menu, with a short form: first day, last day, diagnosis.
- Each entry saves who recorded it, the dates, the diagnosis and when it was recorded.
- Staff see only their own entries. HR sees everyone's.
- **The app can't tell HR apart from other staff yet.** Right now everyone who signs in sees the same things, so an engineer has to add an "HR" role.
- It won't send emails or take photo uploads.

## Review needed

🔴 **This needs an engineer review before it goes live**, because it stores staff health information (the diagnosis).

## Company rules this touches

- **Health data needs written OK first.** A diagnosis is health information, so the person responsible for staff health data has to agree in writing before anything is built. That person hasn't been named yet.
- **Keep only what's needed.** Does HR need the diagnosis, or just a note that a doctor's note came in? Dropping the diagnosis removes the sign-off above and makes this much simpler to approve.
- **Not kept forever.** We need to agree how long entries are kept.
- **Official records.** If this list replaces the emails as HR's official sickness record, the owner of those records must agree to that.

I've noted all four in the idea as "waiting for" the right person.

## What I need from you

Run **/yolo-sdlc:shape** again and tell me:

1. **The examples:** are they right, does one need changing, or is something missing?
2. **The health-data sign-off:** have they already agreed, will you ask them first, or should we drop the diagnosis so it isn't needed?
3. **Who the data owner is, and how long entries should be kept.**

Once you've approved the examples and the sign-off is sorted, I'll mark the idea as agreed and you can move on to **/yolo-sdlc:build**.

report.reply:
Here's how delivery has gone, based on the last merged pull requests. There are only 3 so far.

| Stage | Metric | Value | Based on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Plan | idea → examples agreed (median) | 20 min | 3 PRs |
| 2 Design | changes whose examples were reworked after the build started | 33% | 3 PRs |
| 3 Build | verification passed first time (no verifier round) | 67% | 3 PRs |
| 3 Build | plan → built (median) | 50 min | 3 PRs |
| 4 Test | first ci run passed | 67% | 3 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | pull request open → merged (median) | 30 min | 3 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | reviews with warnings | 50% | 2 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | warnings shipped as they were (last review, total) | 2 | 2 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | merges to main per week (deploys) | 3.0 | 3 PRs |
| 6 Maintain | changes that came from a problem report | 0% | 3 PRs |

**What it means:**

- **Nothing so far came from what users reported.** Every change started as someone's own idea, and none came through the app's "Report a problem" button. That's the clearest gap. **What to try:** run `/yolo-sdlc:triage` to turn any waiting reports into draft ideas.
- **2 review warnings went live without being fixed.** It's a small number, but ask an engineer to look at both and decide whether either matters, before more pile up.
- **Most of the process is quick.** Agreeing examples takes about 20 minutes, building about 50, and a pull request is merged about 30 minutes after it opens. That's roughly 3 changes going live per week.
- **1 in 3 changes hit a snag at each of three points:** the examples changed after the build started, the first verification round failed, or the first automatic check on the pull request (CI) failed. It's too early to tell if these form a pattern.

**What the numbers can't show:**

- **The sample is tiny.** Each percentage is based on 2–3 changes, so a single change moves a number by 33–50 points. Wait for 10 or more before reading trends.
- **Older work has no timings.** Anything built before these steps were in use has no stage times, so it isn't counted here.

This report only reads existing records. Nothing in the app, its labels or its pull requests was changed.
